Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 19, verses 3–6:

Qatada said: he complained of the loss of his molars. ﴿"And my head has glistened with grey hair"﴾, meaning the hair of his head turned white ﴿"mixed with grey"﴾. ﴿"And I have never been unsuccessful in my supplication to You, my Lord"﴾. He means: You have accustomed me to answering in the past, and You have never disappointed me.

It was also said: the meaning is, when You called me to faith, I believed, and I would not be wretched by abandoning faith.[[Omitted from manuscript "A".]]

Al-Kalbi said: the heirs.[[These meanings are close: the heirs are the 'asaba, paternal cousins are among the heirs, and all of them are relatives.]] ﴿"from behind me"﴾, meaning after my death.

Ibn Kathir recited ﴿"min warā'ī"﴾ with a fatha on the ya'; the others recited it with sukun on it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 19, verse 11–13:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿So he came out to his people from the prayer niche﴾. The people used to be behind the prayer niche, waiting for him to open the door for them so that they could enter and pray. Then Zakariyya came out to them with his complexion changed, and they disapproved of him and said, "What is the matter with you, O Zakariyya?" ﴿Then he signaled to them﴾, meaning he gestured to them. Mujahid said: he wrote for them on the ground. ﴿To glorify [Allah]﴾, that is, to pray to Allah, ﴿in the morning and the evening﴾, morning (ghuduwah) and evening. Its meaning is that he used to come out to his people in the morning and the evening and command them to pray. When the time came for his wife to conceive, he was prevented from speaking, so he came out to them and commanded them to pray by gesture.

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿O Yahya﴾. It has been said that there is an ellipsis in it, meaning: "We granted him Yahya, and We said to him: O Yahya." ﴿Take the Scripture﴾, meaning the Torah, ﴿with strength﴾, with earnestness. ﴿And We gave him judgment﴾. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: prophethood. ﴿While a boy﴾, and he was three years old.

It has also been said: by judgment is meant understanding of the Scripture (and this is the preferred view of al-Tabari and other scholars), so he read the Torah while he was young.

It is reported from some of the early scholars (al-salaf): whoever recites the Qur'an before reaching puberty is among those who were given judgment while a boy. [Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in "Shu'ab al-Iman" from Ibn Abbas as a marfu' report. Also narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Daylami as a mawquf report on Ibn Abbas. See: "al-Durr al-Manthur": 5/485; "Kashf al-Khafa" by al-Ajluni: 2/86; Kanz al-Ummal no. (2452).]

﴿And compassion from Us﴾, meaning mercy from Us. Al-Hutay'ah said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: "Show compassion to me, may the King guide you... for every situation has its appropriate speech," meaning: show mercy. [See: "Diwan al-Hutay'ah" p. 222; "Tafsir al-Tabari": 16/57; "al-Bahr al-Muhit": 6/177.]

﴿And purity﴾. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: by zakah is meant obedience and sincerity.

Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is righteous deeds, and this is also the view of al-Dahhak.

The meaning of the verse: We gave him mercy from Us and compassion toward the servants, so that he would call them to obedience to their Lord and act righteously with sincerity.

Al-Kalbi said: meaning a charity which Allah gave in charity on his behalf to his parents.

﴿And he was devout﴾, muslim, sincere and obedient. Among his piety was that he did not commit a sin nor did he intend to commit one. [Al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 16/58; Ahmad in "al-Zuhd", Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim, from Qatadah who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib used to say: the Prophet ﷺ said: "No one meets Allah on the Day of Resurrection without a sin, except Yahya ibn Zakariyya." And al-Hasan said: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Yahya ibn Zakariyya never committed a sin, nor did he intend to be with a woman." Both are mursal. See: "al-Durr al-Manthur": 5/486-487; "Tafsir Ibn Kathir": 3/114-115, where he cited these reports and others and pointed out their weakness.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 19, verse 23:

﴿So the pains of childbirth drove her﴾, i.e., compelled her and brought her, ﴿to the trunk of the palm tree﴾ (al-makhad), which is the pain of childbirth. ﴿to the trunk of the palm tree﴾. It was a dry palm tree in the desert, in the severe cold of winter, and it had no fronds.

It was also said: she leaned against it to support herself and hold on to it because of the pain of childbirth. ﴿She said: "Would that I had died before this"﴾. She wished for death out of shame before people and fear of disgrace. ﴿"And I had been a thing forgotten"﴾. Hamzah and Hafs read ﴿nasyan﴾ with a fatha on the nun, [and the rest (of the readers) with a kasra on it] [[The text between the brackets is missing from manuscript "a".]]. The two are dialectal variants, like al-watr and al-witr, and al-jisr and al-jisr. It means "the thing forgotten." And "nasy" in the lexicon means: anything that is cast away and forgotten and not mentioned because of its insignificance.

﴿Forgotten﴾, i.e., abandoned. Qatadah said: a thing that is not known and not mentioned. 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: a cast-off corpse. It was also said: it means "I had not been created."

﴿So he called to her from beneath her﴾. Abu Ja'far, Nafi', Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs recited ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ (min tahtiha) with a kasra on the mim and the ta', meaning Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him. Maryam was on a hillock (akamah) and Jibril was behind the hillock, beneath her, and he called to her.

The others recited it with a fatha on the mim and the ta', and they also meant Jibril, peace be upon him. He called to her from the foot of the mountain.

It was also said that it was Isa (Jesus), who, when he came out of his mother's womb, called to her: ﴿Do not grieve﴾. This is the view of Mujahid and al-Hasan. [[Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari in his tafsir (16/68) preferred this view, because the pronoun referring to Isa is closer than the one referring to Jibril, and the closer reference should be preferred over the more distant one. Do you not see that in the context of His saying, ﴿So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a remote place﴾, meaning: she carried Isa and withdrew with him; then it says ﴿Then he called to her﴾ as a continuation of the reference to Isa and the report about him? There is also another reason: His saying ﴿Then she pointed to him﴾. She would not have pointed to him, God willing, unless she knew that he was able to speak at that very moment, because of what she had come to know and trust from him when he addressed her, saying: ﴿Do not grieve; your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾. And God did not report that he told her: "Point to him to the people." If that had been a statement from Jibril, it would have been fitting for the outward report to make clear that Isa would speak and plead on her behalf to the people, and that he would instruct her to point to him for the people when they asked her about her condition and his.]]

The first view is the statement of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, al-Suddi, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and a group, that the one calling was Jibril, when he heard her speech and recognised her distress, and called to her: ﴿Do not grieve﴾.

﴿Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾. The word "al-sari" (stream) means a small river.

It was also said: "beneath you" means that Allah placed it under your command, so that if you ordered it to flow, it would flow, and if you ordered it to stop, it would stop.

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Jibril, peace be upon him, struck the ground with his foot (and it is said: Isa, peace and blessings be upon him, struck it with his foot), and a spring of sweet water appeared and flowed.

[[See Tafsir al-Khazin: 4/197.]]

It was also said: there was a dry river there, and Allah, glorified and exalted, caused water to flow in it, and the dry palm tree came to life, so it put forth leaves, bore fruit and ripened into dates.

al-Hasan said: "beneath you a stream" refers to Isa, and by Allah he was a noble servant (abdan sariyyan), meaning elevated.

[[Al-Tabari (16/71) preferred the first view, saying: "The more correct of the two views in my opinion is the view of the one who said it refers to the stream, because He informed her of the water that Allah had given her, the water He had placed beside her, and said to her: ﴿And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates. So eat﴾ of these dates, ﴿and drink﴾ from this water, ﴿and be comforted in your eye﴾ by your child. And 'al-sari' is well known in the speech of the Arabs as the small river." Some prophetic reports have been transmitted concerning this, none of which is sound, although it is the closer to the truth than the view of those who said that "al-sari" means Isa, peace be upon him, even though one of the meanings of "al-sari" is one of high rank. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 19, verse 25–26:

﴿And shake towards you﴾ meaning: it was said to Maryam, "Move" ﴿the trunk of the palm tree﴾. The Arabs say, "hazzahu" and "hazza bihi," just as they say "hazza ra'sahu" and "hazza bi-ra'sihi," and "amdada al-habla" and "amdada bihi" (he stretched the rope). ﴿It will drop upon you﴾: the well-known reading is with a fatha on the ta' and the qaf and a shadda on the sin, meaning "tatasaqqatu" (it falls down repeatedly), and one of the two ta's was assimilated into the sin, meaning: the palm tree will drop upon you ripe dates. Hamzah lightened the sin and deleted the ta' which the others had assimilated.

Hafs read with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the qaf, lightened, on the pattern of "tafa'ala." "Tusaqit" has the meaning of "asqata" (to make fall), and the feminine form is due to "al-nakhlah" (the palm tree).

Ya'qub read "yassaqatu" with a ya' and a shadda, returning it to the trunk (al-jidh).

﴿Fresh ripe dates﴾: "janiyyan," meaning "majniyyan" (picked). It was also said: al-janyu is that which has reached its full stage and the time for its picking has come. Al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym said: "Nothing is better for the woman who has given birth than dates, and nothing is better for the sick than honey." [[Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir; see "al-Durr al-Manthur": 5/505.]]

His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿So eat and drink﴾ meaning: so eat, O Maryam, of the dates, and drink from the water of the river. ﴿And be comforted﴾ meaning: be content of soul. It was also said: "Cool your eye with your son Isa." It is said: "Aqarra Allah 'aynak" meaning: may your heart meet what pleases you, so that your eye is at rest from looking at anything else. It was also said: "Aqarra Allahu 'aynahu" means He made him sleep; it is said "qarra yaqirru" when he settles.

It was also said: when the eye weeps from joy, the tear is cool, and when it weeps from grief, the tear is hot. From this it is said: "Aqarra Allahu 'aynahu" and "Askhana Allahu 'aynahu."

﴿And if you see any human﴾: meaning "tara," and the nun of emphasis entered upon it, so the ya' was kasra due to the meeting of the two sakins.

Its meaning: if you see any human being who asks you about your child, ﴿then say, "I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast"﴾ meaning: silence. Thus Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) used to read it.

Al-sawm in the language means abstaining from food, drink, and speech.

Al-Suddi said: among the Children of Israel, whoever wished to strive would fast from speech just as he fasts from food, so he would not speak until evening.

**Al-Baghawi's Commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 19, verse 29:**

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 19, verse 38–39:

﴿How much they will hear and see﴾ means: how much they will hear and see on the Day of Resurrection, when hearing and sight will not benefit them! He informs that they will hear and see in the Hereafter what they did not hear and did not see in this world.

Al-Kalbi said: "There will be no one on the Day of Resurrection who hears or sees more than them, when Allah the Exalted says to Jesus: ﴿Did you say to the people...﴾" (Qur'an 5:116).

﴿But the wrongdoers today are in clear error, the Day they come to Us﴾ means: in clear mistake. His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿And warn them of the Day of regret, when the matter will be decided﴾ means: the reckoning is finished, the people of Paradise are admitted to Paradise, the people of the Fire to the Fire, and Death is slaughtered.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, ʿAmr ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath informed us, my father informed us, al-Aʿmash informed us, Abu Salih informed us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Death will be brought in the likeness of a white-black ram. A caller will call out: O people of Paradise! They will look up and peer, and he will say: Do you recognize this? They will say: Yes, this is Death, and all of them have seen it. Then he will call: O people of the Fire! They will look up and peer, and he will say: Do you recognize this? They will say: Yes, this is Death, and all of them have seen it. Then it will be slaughtered, and he will say: O people of Paradise, eternal abiding with no death, and O people of the Fire, eternal abiding with no death." Then he recited: ﴿And warn them of the Day of regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are heedless and do not believe﴾.

Abu ʿIsa narrated it from Ahmad ibn Mani', from al-Nadr ibn Isma'il, from al-Aʿmash with this chain, and he added: "Were it not that Allah the Exalted had decreed life and permanence for the people of Paradise, they would die of joy; and were it not that Allah the Exalted had decreed life and permanence for the people of the Fire, they would die of sorrow."

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Mu'adh ibn Asad informed us, ʿAbd Allah informed us, ʿUmar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd informed us, from his father, that he narrated to him from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the people of Paradise have entered Paradise and the people of the Fire have entered the Fire, Death will be brought and placed between Paradise and the Fire. Then it will be slaughtered, and a caller will call: O people of Paradise, no death! O people of the Fire, no death! So the people of Paradise will increase in joy upon their joy, and the people of the Fire will increase in grief upon their grief."

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Abu al-Yaman informed us, Shu'ayb informed us, Abu al-Zinad informed us, from al-Aʿraj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one will enter Paradise without being shown his seat in the Fire, so that he may increase in gratitude if he had done evil; and no one will enter the Fire without being shown his seat in Paradise, had he done good, so that it becomes a regret for him."

Abu al-Hasan ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi informed us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us, al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan informed us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Yahya ibn ʿAbd Allah said: I heard my father say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one dies except that he regrets." They said: "What is his regret, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "If he was a doer of good, he regrets not having increased; and if he was a doer of evil, he regrets not having desisted."

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿while they are heedless﴾ means: of what will be done to them in the Hereafter, ﴿and they do not believe﴾ means: they do not affirm.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And mention in the Book Idris﴾. He is the grandfather of Abu Nuh (Noah), and his name is "Akhnukh." He was called Idris because of his frequent study (*dars*) of books. He was a tailor, and he was the first to write with the pen, the first to sew garments, and the first to wear sewn clothing, whereas before him people wore hides. He was also the first to make weapons and to fight the disbelievers, and the first to examine the science of the stars (astronomy) and calculation. ﴿Indeed, he was a truthful one (*siddiq*), a prophet.﴾

And We raised him to a lofty station (﴿وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا﴾). It was said: it means Paradise. And it was said: it means elevation in rank in this world.

It was also said: it means that he was raised to the fourth heaven. [Omitted in manuscript A.]

Anas ibn Malik narrated from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he saw Idris in the fourth heaven on the night of the Mi'raj (Ascension). [A portion of a long hadith recorded by al-Bukhari (7/201-202) and Muslim (1/149-151). Its takhrij (sourcing) was previously given in the commentary on Surat al-Isra'.]

The cause of Idris being raised [to the heaven] [Words in brackets omitted in manuscript A.], according to what Ka'b and others said, was that he went out one day on an errand, and the heat of the sun struck him. He said: "O Lord, I walked for a single day, so how will it be for the one who carries it for a distance of five hundred years in a single day! O Allah, lighten its burden and its heat from him." [He meant the angel entrusted with the sun.] When the angel woke up, he found the sun lighter and less hot than he had known, and he said [i.e., the angel entrusted with it]: "O Lord, what have You decreed concerning this?" He said: "Indeed My servant Idris asked Me to lighten your burden and its heat, and I granted his request." The angel said: "O Lord, make between me and him a close friendship." So He permitted him, and he came to Idris, who would ask him [for things]. Idris said to him: "I have been informed that you are the most honored of the angels and the most esteemed in the sight of the Angel of Death. So intercede for me with him, that he may postpone my term, so that I may increase in gratitude and worship." The angel said: "Allah does not postpone a soul when its term has come, but I will speak to him." Then he raised him to the heaven and placed him at the rising place of the sun. Then he went to the Angel of Death and said: "I have a need of you: a friend of mine from the children of Adam has asked me to intercede with you that you postpone his term." He said: "That is not up to me, but if you wish, I will inform him of his term, so that he may prepare for his soul." He said: "Yes." So he looked in his register and said: "You have spoken to me about a man whom I do not see ever dying." He said: "How so?" He said: "I do not find him dying except at the rising place of the sun." He said: "Then I came to you and left him there." He said: "Go, and I do not think you will find him except that he has died. By Allah, nothing of Idris's term remains." The angel returned and found him dead.

[This narration was related by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (11/118), and by Ibn al-Jawzi in "Zad al-Masir" (5/243), who said: "This meaning is related from Ibn Abbas and Ka'b, among others." Ibn Kathir commented on these narrations and similar ones, saying that they contain strangeness and rejection, and that they are among the reports of Ka'b al-Ahbar from the Isra'iliyyat (Israelite narratives, reports of Jewish and Christian origin transmitted into Islamic exegesis). See: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (3/127).]

They differed as to whether he is alive in the heaven or dead. Some people said: he is dead. Others said: he is alive. [The first opinion agrees with the narrations; the second is related from Mujahid, who said: Idris was raised and did not die, just as Jesus was raised. If he meant that he has not died until now, there is room for scrutiny in this; but if he meant that he was raised alive to the heaven and then took his soul there, then this does not contradict what was previously related from Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Allah knows best. See: "al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya" by Ibn Kathir (1/100).] They said: four of the prophets are alive: two on the earth, al-Khidr and Ilyas; and two in the heaven, Idris and Jesus.

Wahb said: For Idris, each day, there was raised for him as much worship as was raised for all the people of the earth in his time. The angels marveled at him, and the Angel of Death longed for him, so he asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, for permission to visit him, and He permitted him. So he came to him in the form of a son of Adam. Idris used to fast continually, so when it was time for his breaking of the fast, he invited him to his food, but he refused to eat with him. He did this for three nights, and Idris disapproved of him. So on the third night he said to him: "I want to know who you are." He said: "I am the Angel of Death; I asked my Lord for permission to accompany you." He said: "Then I have a need of you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "That you take my soul." So Allah revealed to him: "Take his soul." So he took his soul, and Allah returned it to him after an hour. The Angel of Death said to him: "What was your purpose in asking me to take the soul?" He said: "To taste the anguish and the distress of death, so that I may be better prepared for it." Then Idris said to him: "I have another need of you." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "That you raise me to the heaven, so that I may look at it, and at Paradise and Hell." So Allah permitted his elevation. When he drew near Hell, he said to him: "I have another need." He said: "And what do you want?" He said: "That you ask Malik [the keeper of Hell] to open its gates for me, so that I may see it." He did so. Then he said: "Since you have shown me Hell, show me Paradise." So he took him to Paradise and asked for it to be opened, and Allah revealed to him: "Take his soul." So he took his soul, and Allah returned it to him after an hour. The Angel of Death said to him: "What is in..." [the text here is broken in the source] Its gates were opened, and he admitted him into Paradise. Then the Angel of Death said: "Come out, so that you may return to your abode." But he clung to a tree and said: "I will not come out of it." So Allah sent a wise angel between them. The angel said to him: "Why will you not come out?" He said: "Because Allah, Exalted, said: 'Every soul shall taste death' (Al 'Imran 3:185), and I have tasted it; and He said: 'There is none of you but will pass over it' (Maryam 19:71), and I have passed over it; and He said: 'And they will never be removed from it' (al-Hijr 15:48), so I will not leave." Then Allah revealed to the Angel of Death, by My permission he entered Paradise, and by My command he will not come out; so he is alive there. That is the meaning of His saying, Exalted: ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾.

[See: "al-Durr al-Manthur" (5/519-523) and "Zad al-Masir" (5/241-242). This report is from the Isra'iliyyat, and Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, pointed this out.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 19, verse 58:

﴿Those are the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor from among the prophets, of the descendants of Adam﴾, i.e., Idris and Nuh (Noah). ﴿And of those whom We carried with Nuh﴾, i.e., and of the descendants of those whom We carried with Nuh in the ark, meaning Ibrahim (Abraham), because he was born of Sam ibn Nuh (Shem son of Noah). ﴿And of the descendants of Ibrahim﴾, meaning Isma'il (Ishmael), Ishaq (Isaac) and Ya'qub (Jacob).

His saying: ﴿And Isra'il (Israel)﴾, i.e., and of the descendants of Isra'il, who are Musa (Moses), Harun (Aaron), Zakariyya (Zechariah), Yahya (John) and Isa (Jesus).

His saying: ﴿And of those whom We guided and chose﴾, these were among those whom We guided and selected. ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down prostrating and weeping﴾. "Sujjadan" (prostrating): the plural of sajid (one who prostrates); "bukiyyan" (weeping): the plural of baki (one who weeps). Allah informed that the prophets, whenever they heard the signs of Allah, would prostrate and weep.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 19, verse 59:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Then there succeeded them a posterity﴾. That is, after the aforementioned prophets there succeeded a posterity (khalf) who were evil people. "Khalf" with a fatha (khalf) means the righteous, and with a sukun (khalf) means the wicked. [[This is the view of Ibn al-A'rabi, and they cited for it the verse of Labid: "Gone are those with whom one lived in their shelter, and I remain among a later generation (khalf) like the mangy hide..." And from this comes the saying about poor speech: khalf. And from it the well-known proverb: "He remained silent a thousand times and spoke one khalf." So khalf with sukun is used in dispraise and khalf with fatha in praise; this is the commonly known usage. The Prophet ﷺ said: "This knowledge will be carried by the trustworthy from every khalf (generation)..." (narrated by al-Bayhaqi; Imam Ahmad said: there is no harm in it). Each of the two may sometimes be used in place of the other. Hassan ibn Thabit said: "For us is the first precedence towards You, and a khalf (later one) who repented in obedience to God for the first of us..." Another said: "Indeed we found a khalf, an evil khalf, who closed his door on us and then swore..." "The doorkeeper admits only one who is known, a servant who, when he stumbles under the load, stands still." See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/310-311, and refer to what preceded in the tafsir of Surat al-A'raf, verse (169).]].

Al-Suddi said: He meant by them the Jews and those who joined them.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: they are within this community (ummah). [[See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/122; Zad al-Masir: 5/245; and al-Suyuti cited a number of reports on this: 5/526. That they are from the community of Muhammad ﷺ is not convincing according to Shaykh al-Shinqiti, because the Most High's saying "Then there succeeded them" is a form indicating occurrence in the past, and it cannot be turned to the future except by a proof that must be relied upon, as you see. The apparent meaning is that they are the Jews, the Christians and other disbelievers who succeeded their prophets and righteous people before the revelation of the verse, so they neglected the prayer and followed desires. In any case, the lesson is in the generality of the wording, not the specific cause; so every posterity who neglected the prayer and followed desires falls under the reproach and threat mentioned in this verse, and the following of desires mentioned in the verse is general to following every desire that distracts from the remembrance of God and from prayer. See: Adwa' al-Bayan: 4/308.]].

﴿They neglected the prayer﴾: they abandoned the obligatory prayer. [[This is related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and it was chosen by al-Zajjaj. See: al-Tabari: 16/98; Zad al-Masir: 5/245; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/526.]]

Ibn Mas'ud and Ibrahim said: they delayed it from its time.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: it is that one does not pray the noon prayer until the afternoon comes, nor the afternoon prayer until the sun sets. [[This is related from al-Qasim ibn Makhimarah, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Nakha'i and Mujahid. Moreover, everything reported from the early generations, may God have mercy on them, concerning the interpretation of the verse falls within its meaning, because delaying it beyond its time, not establishing it in congregation, neglecting its conditions, denying its obligation, and leaving the mosques empty of it, all of these are sayings in the interpretation of the verse, and all of them are neglect of it, although the kinds of neglect vary. See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/122-125; Adwa' al-Bayan: 4/308.]]

﴿And followed their desires﴾: that is, sins and drinking wine; meaning they preferred the desires of their souls over obedience to God. Mujahid said: these are a people who will appear at the end of time, who will leap upon one another in the markets and alleys.

﴿So they will encounter Ghayy﴾. Wahb said: "Ghayy" is a river in Hell, deep in its bed and foul in its taste.

Ibn Abbas said: "Ghayy" is a valley in Hell, and the valleys of Hell seek refuge from its heat; it is prepared for the adulterer who persists in it, the wine-drinker who is addicted to it, the eater of usury who does not desist from it, the disobedient to parents, and the false witness. [[See: al-Qurtubi: 11/125.]]

Ata' said: "Ghayy" is a valley in Hell that flows with pus and blood.

Ka'b said: it is a valley in Hell, the furthest of it in depth and the fiercest of it in heat, in a well called "al-Him"; whenever Hell subsides, God opens that well and Hell is kindled by it. [[See al-Qurtubi, ibid.]]

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah related to us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Harithi related to us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i related to us: Abdullah ibn Mahmud related to us: Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khallal related to us; and Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Hushaym ibn Bashir, who said: Zakariyya ibn Abi Maryam al-Khuza'i related to us, saying: I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: "The distance between the brink of Hell and its bottom is seventy autumns' journey for a stone that falls, or he said a rock that falls, whose size is like ten fat bones..." A client of Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn al-Walid said to him: "Is there anything beneath that, O Abu Umamah?" He said: "Yes, Ghayy and Athham." [[Similar was related from Abu Umamah as a marfu' report by al-Tabari in his tafsir: 16/100; al-Suyuti added its attribution to Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqi in "al-Ba'th", and al-Tabarani. Al-Haythami said in "al-Majma'" (10/389): "It contains weak narrators, though Ibn Hibban declared them trustworthy and said they err." Ibn Kathir said (3/129): "This is a strange hadith, and its marfu' form is munkar."]]

Al-Dahhak said: Ghayy means perdition and loss. It was also said: destruction. It was said: punishment. [[Al-Tabari said (16/100): "All these sayings are close in meaning, for whoever enters the two wells that the Prophet ﷺ mentioned and the valley that Ibn Mas'ud mentioned in Hell, having entered it, has met with loss and evil..."]]

His saying: ﴿So they will encounter Ghayy﴾ does not mean merely that they will see it, but rather it means being gathered together with it and being in direct contact with it, alongside seeing it. [[In "B" it reads "al-mulamasah" (touching).]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 19, verses 60–62:**

﴿Except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds. Those will enter Paradise, and they will not be wronged in the least.﴾

﴿Gardens of Eden, which the Most Merciful has promised to His servants in the unseen﴾, though they have not seen them, ﴿indeed His promise is ever coming to pass.﴾ That is, ﴿آتِيًا﴾ (ātiyan, "coming to pass") means ﴿مَأْتِيًّا﴾ (ma'tiyan) is ﴿مَفْعُولٌ﴾ (maf'ūl, passive form) used with the meaning of ﴿فَاعِلٍ﴾ (fā'il, active form).

It was also said: He did not say ﴿آتِيًا﴾ because whoever comes to you, you have come to him. The Arabs do not distinguish between the speaker's saying "fifty years have come upon me" (atat ʿalayya khamsūna sanatan) and his saying "I have come upon fifty years" (ataytu ʿalā khamsīna sanatan). And they say: "good has reached me" (waṣala ilayya al-khayr) and "I have reached good" (waṣaltu ilā al-khayr).

Ibn Jarir said: "His promise" means His promised thing, which is Paradise, ﴿مَأْتِيًّا﴾ "to be come to," which His friends [the people of Paradise] [[Addition from "B" and not in al-Tabari.]] and the people of His obedience come to. [[The wording of al-Tabari in the tafsir (16/101): "Indeed Allah... and His promise in this place: His promised thing, which is Paradise, 'to be come to,' which His friends and the people of His obedience come to, whom Allah causes to enter it. Some grammarians of Kufa said: The statement is made such that the promise is the thing to be come to, and its meaning is: it is He who comes. He did not say 'and His promise was coming,' because everything that comes to you, you come to it. Do you not see that you say: 'I have come upon fifty years,' and 'fifty years have come upon me,' and both are correct..."]]

﴿They will not hear therein﴾ in Paradise ﴿any vain talk﴾ (laghwan), meaning falsehood, obscenity, and superfluous speech.

Muqatil said: It is the false oath.

﴿Except a greeting (salāman)﴾. This is an exception from a different category, meaning: rather, they will hear therein "greeting," that is, speech from which they are safe. "Al-salām" (peace) is a comprehensive term for good, because it includes safety.

Its meaning is: the people of Paradise do not hear what would make them sinful; they only hear what brings them peace.

It was also said: it is the greeting of some of them to others, and the greeting of the angels to them.

It was also said: it is Allah's greeting to them.

﴿And for them their provision therein, morning and evening.﴾ The people of tafsir said: There is no night in Paradise by which morning and evening are known. Rather, they are always in light, but they receive their provisions according to the measure of the two ends of the day.

It was also said: they know the time of day by the raising of the veils and the time of night by the lowering of the veils.

It was also said: what is meant is the ease of life and abundance of provision without restriction.

Al-Hasan al-Basri used to say: The Arabs did not know of any better living than provision in the morning and evening, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, described His Paradise with that.

[[See these sayings and a number of reports on this in: al-Durr al-Manthur (5/528–529) and Tafsir Ibn Kathir (3/120–121).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 19, verses 70–71:

﴿Then We are most knowing of those most deserving of burning therein.﴾ That is: most deserving of entering the Fire. It is said: ṣaliya yaṣlā ṣilīyan (صَلِيَ يَصْلَى صِلِيًّا), like laqiya yalqā liqiyyan (لَقِيَ يَلْقَى لِقِيًّا), and ṣalā yaṣlī ṣuliyyan (صَلَى يَصْلِي صُلِيًّا), like maḍā yamḍī muḍiyyan (مَضَى يَمْضِي مُضِيًّا), meaning he entered the Fire and endured its heat.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it.﴾ Meaning: there is none of you but will come to it. It is said that the oath is implied within it, meaning: "By Allah, there is none of you but will come to it." Al-wurud (الْوُرُودُ) is arriving at a place.

The scholars differed about the meaning of al-wurud here, and about what the pronoun in His saying ﴿wāriduhā﴾ refers to. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), and it is the view of the majority, said: the meaning of al-wurud here is entering, and the pronoun refers to the Fire. They said: the Fire will be entered by the righteous and the wicked; then Allah will save those who had taqwa (الذين اتقوا) and bring them out of it.

The evidence that al-wurud means entering is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, quoting Pharaoh: "He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them down into the Fire" (Hud: 98).

Ibn 'Uyaynah related from 'Amr ibn Dinar that Nafi' ibn al-Azraq disputed with Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) about al-wurud. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: it is entering. Nafi' said: al-wurud is not entering. Then Abdullah ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) recited His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship other than Allah are firewood for Hell; you will be arriving at it﴾ (al-Anbiya: 98), [and asked]: "Did these enter it or not?" Then he said: "O Nafi', by Allah, you and I will come to it, and I hope that Allah will bring me out of it, and I do not think that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will bring you out of it because of your denial."

Others said: al-wurud does not mean entering. They said: a believer never enters the Fire, due to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us – they will be kept far from it. They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ (al-Anbiya: 101–102). They said: whoever enters it does not leave it. The meaning of His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ is presence and sight, not entering, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan﴾ (al-Qasas: 23), meaning he arrived there. [This is the view of 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr.]

'Ikrimah said: the verse refers to the disbelievers, for they enter it and do not leave it. [Also related from Ibn 'Abbas.]

It was related from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ means: the Resurrection, and the pronoun refers to it.

The first view is more sound, and it is the view of Ahl al-Sunnah: that all of them enter the Fire, then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings out from it the people of faith, by the evidence of His saying, Exalted is He:

The first view is more sound, and it is the view of Ahl al-Sunnah: that all of them enter the Fire, then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings out from it the people of faith, by the evidence of His saying, Exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 19, verse 72 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Then We shall save those who were mindful of God﴾, that is, who were mindful of associating partners with God (shirk), and they are the believers. The address is general, concerning both believers and disbelievers, and they differed over the interpretation of "warid" (coming to it) in five opinions: the first is entering it; the second is passing by it; the third is being present at it; the fourth is that the coming of the Muslims to it is their passing over the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), and the coming of the polytheists is their entering the Fire; and the fifth is that the coming of the believers to it is the fever they suffer in this world. See: Zad al-Masir: (5 / 254-257). The most preferred of these opinions is that of al-Tabari, may God have mercy on him, where he said (16 / 112): "All of them will come to it, then the believers will depart from it, God will save them, and the disbelievers will fall into it. Then he cited the hadiths... This is also what the author of Sharh al-Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah preferred, when he said (p. 478): "The most apparent and strongest view is that it is passing over the Sirat." See also: Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3 / 132-134; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 6 / 209-210.]].

Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read "nunji" with light (single) emphasis, and the others read it with the doubled letter (intensive form).

The evidence for this is what Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi informed us, that Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us, that Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us, that Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib informed us, that Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "No Muslim loses three children and then enters the Fire, except for the fulfilment of the oath" [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Aiman wa al-Nudhur, chapter on the saying of God Most High: "And they swore by God with their most emphatic oaths" (11 / 541), and Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Silah wa al-Adab, chapter on the virtue of one who loses a child and seeks reward for it, no. (2632): 4 / 2028, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5 / 451.]].

By "the oath" he meant His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will come to it﴾.

O Most Bountiful!' Then God, Mighty and Majestic, will say to Gabriel: 'Go and bring Me this servant of Mine.' He said: So Gabriel went and found the people of the Fire prostrate and weeping. He returned and informed his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. He said: 'Go, for he is in such and such a place.' He said: So he brought him. He said: 'O My servant, how did you find your place and your resting place?' He said: 'O Lord, the worst of places and the worst of resting places.' He said: 'Return My servant.' He said: 'I did not expect that You would return me to it after You had brought me out of it.' God Most High said to His angels: 'Leave My servant.'" It was also said: kneeling on their knees. Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, that Ahmad al-Nu'aimi informed us, that Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, that Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, that Abu al-Yaman informed us, that Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who informed me: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Ata' ibn Yazid al-Laythi, that Abu Hurayrah informed them both that the people said: "O Messenger of God, shall we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Do you have any difficulty seeing the sun when there is no cloud between you and it?" They said: "No." He said: "You will see Him in the same way. This community will remain, with its hypocrites among them, and God, Mighty and Majestic, will come to them and say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'We are in this place until our Lord comes to us, and when our Lord comes we will recognize Him.' Then God will come to them and say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'You are our Lord.' He will call them, and the Sirat (bridge) will be set up between the backs of Hell. I will be the first of the Messengers to pass over with my community, and on that day none will speak except the Messengers, and the speech of the Messengers on that day will be: 'O God, keep us safe, keep us safe!' In Hell there are hooks like the thorns of the sa'dan plant. Have you seen the thorns of the sa'dan?" They said: "Yes." He said: "They are like the thorns of the sa'dan, except that none knows their size except God. They snatch people by their deeds. They bring them out and recognize them by the marks of prostration, and God has forbidden the Fire to consume the mark of prostration. So they come out of the Fire, for every son of Adam is consumed by the Fire except the mark of prostration. They come out of the Fire having been burned (imtahashu) [[That is, burned.]], so the water of life is poured over them, and they grow like a seed grows in the flood-debris (hamil al-sayl) [[The "hibbah" is the seed of herbs and grasses that grows in the wilderness and along the edges of floods, and its plural is "hubb"; "hamil al-sayl" is what the flood carries of mud or debris.]]. Then God will finish the judgement among the servants, and one man will remain between Paradise and the Fire, the last of the people of the Fire to enter Paradise, facing toward the Fire. He will say: 'O Lord, turn my face away from the Fire, for its smell has poisoned me and its flame has burned me.' God will say: 'Perhaps if I do that for you, you will ask for something else?' He will say: 'No, by Your might.' So he gives to God whatever God wills of covenant and pledge, and God turns his face away from the Fire. When he turns toward Paradise and sees its brightness, he remains silent as long as God wills him to be silent. Then he says: 'O Lord, bring me forward to the gate of Paradise.' God, Blessed and Exalted, will say: 'Did you not give covenants and pledges that you would not ask for anything other than what you had asked?' He will say: 'O Lord, do not let me be the most wretched of Your creation.' He will say: 'What if I give you that, will you ask for something else?' He will say: 'No, by Your might, I will not ask You for anything other than that.' So he gives his Lord whatever he wills of covenant and pledge, and He brings him forward to the gate of Paradise. When he reaches its gate and sees its splendour and what is in it of delight and joy, he remains silent as long as God wills him to be silent. Then he says: 'O Lord, admit me into Paradise.' God Most High will say: 'Woe to you, O son of Adam, how treacherous you are! Did you not give covenants and pledges that you would not ask for anything other than what you were given?' He says: 'O Lord, do not make me the most wretched of Your creation.' Then God laughs at him, and then permits him to enter Paradise, and says: 'Wish.' So he wishes, until his wishes are exhausted. God Most High says: 'Wish for such and such.' He begins to remind him, until his desires come to an end, and God Most High says: 'For you is that, and the like of it with it.'" Abu Sa'id said to Abu Hurayrah: "The Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'God Most High says: That is for you, and ten times its like.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "I did not memorize from the Messenger of God ﷺ except his saying: 'For you is that, and the like of it with it.'" Abu Sa'id said: "I heard him say: 'That is for you, and ten times its like.'" [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Tawhid, chapter on the saying of God Most High: "Faces that Day will be radiant" (13 / 419-420); Muslim in al-Iman, chapter on knowing the way to the vision (of God), no. (182): 1 / 163-167; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15 / 173.]]

God will then come to them in the form they recognize, and say: 'I am your Lord.' They will say: 'You are our Lord,' and they will follow Him." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, chapter "The Sirat is the bridge of Hell" (11 / 444-445).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 19, verse 72 (part 2 of 2):

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi related to us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Hiri related to us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi related to us: Muhammad ibn Hammad related to us: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Some people from among the People of Monotheism (ahl al-tawhid) will be punished in the Fire until they become charred coals. He said: "The people of Paradise will sprinkle water on them, and they will sprout as the cucumber (qitha') sprouts in the debris carried by a flood. Then they will enter Paradise."

Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Samad al-Jawzajani related to us: Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i related to us: Abu Sa'id al-Haytham ibn Kulayb related to us: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi related to us: Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ubayda al-Salmani, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, I know the last of the people of the Fire to come out of it. So he will return and say: 'My Lord, the people have taken the abodes.' It will be said to him: 'Do you remember the time when you were in it?' He will say: 'Yes.' It will be said to him: 'Wish.' He will wish, and it will be said to him: 'Indeed, for you is what you have wished for, and ten times the like of the world.' He will say: 'Do you mock me while You are the King?'" Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi related to us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri related to us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi related to us: Muhammad ibn Hammad related to us: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, from Hafsa (may Allah be pleased with her), that she said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, I hope that, if Allah wills, no one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyya will enter the Fire." She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, has not Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it; that is ever a decree decreed by your Lord﴾?" He said: "Have you not heard Him say: ﴿Then We will save those who feared Allah, and We will leave the wrongdoers therein kneeling﴾?"

[Related by Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, chapter "Mention of the Resurrection": 2/1431; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 6/285; Hannad in al-Zuhd: 1/328; Ibn Jarir in al-Tafsir: 16/112; Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah: 2/414. It was also related by another route by Imam Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahaba, in a similar form, under no. (2496): 4/1942, and by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 6/420, and the author recorded it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/193.]

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 19, verses 73–74:**

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, clear ones﴾ [[Variant: "bayyinat" = "clear."]] ﴿those who disbelieved say﴾, meaning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and his kinsmen from Quraysh, ﴿to those who believed﴾, meaning the poor [[In "A": "nafaran min" (a group of).]] Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ). They had austerity, roughness in their living, and shabbiness in their clothing. The polytheists would comb their hair, oil their heads, and wear the silk of garments. So they said to the believers: ﴿Which of the two groups is better in position (maqaman)﴾, meaning in dwelling and abode, [and maqam is the place of residence.

Ibn Kathir recited "muqaman" with a damma on the mim, meaning "iqamatan" (residence)] [[Omitted in "A".]].

﴿And better in assembly (nadiyyan)﴾, meaning in gathering. Its like is al-nadi (the assembly place). So Allah, exalted is He, answered them, saying: ﴿How many generations have We destroyed before them who were better in furnishing (athathan) and appearance (ri'yan)?﴾ Athathan means goods and wealth. Muqatil said: it means clothing and garments. ﴿Ri'yan﴾: most of the reciters read it with a hamza, meaning appearance (manzaran), from "al-ru'yah" (sight). Ibn 'Amir, Abu Ja'far, and Nafi', other than Warsh, read "wariyyan" with a shaddah and without a hamza. It has two interpretations: the first is the same as the former, with the hamza dropped. The second is from "al-rayy," which is the opposite of thirst, and its meaning is satiation with blessing, for the one living in luxury shows the satiation of blessing, while the poor show the trailing skirts of poverty.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 19, verses 75–78:

﴿Say: "Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend his term."﴾ This is a command with the meaning of a statement. Its meaning is: He leaves him in his transgression and gives him respite in his disbelief. ﴿Until, when they see what they are promised, either the punishment﴾, which is capture and killing in this world, ﴿or the Hour﴾, meaning the Resurrection, ﴿then they will know who is worse in position﴾ (*makanan*, in rank) ﴿and weaker in forces﴾, having fewer helpers. Is it they, or the believers? Because they are in the Fire and the believers are in Paradise. This is a refutation of them in His saying: ﴿Which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly?﴾

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And Allah increases those who are guided in guidance﴾, that is, in faith and certainty upon their certainty. [10/a] ﴿And the enduring good deeds﴾ are the remembrances (*adhkar*) and the righteous deeds that remain for their doer, ﴿are better with your Lord in reward and better in return﴾, meaning in outcome and final destination.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, ʿAmr ibn Hafs informed us, my father informed us, al-A'mash ibn Muslim informed us, from Masruq, who said: Khabbab related to us, who said: "I was a smith, and I made (a sword) for al-As ibn Wa'il, and my wealth accumulated with him. I came to him to demand my payment. He said, 'No, by Allah, I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad.' I said, 'Never, by Allah, until you die and are then resurrected.' He said, 'Am I to die and then be resurrected?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Then I will have wealth and children there, and I will pay you.'" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, Surah Maryam, chapter "Nay, We shall record what he says and extend for him of the punishment an extension" (8/430–431). Mujahid said: "Has he known the knowledge of the unseen, so that he knows whether he will be in Paradise or not?" ﴿Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ That is, has he said, "There is no god but Allah"? Qatadah said: That is, a righteous deed he has sent ahead. Al-Kalbi said: "Has a covenant been made with him that he will enter Paradise?"

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 19, verses 84–87:**

﴿So do not be hasty against them﴾, that is, do not hasten to seek their punishment. ﴿We are only counting for them a counting﴾. Al-Kalbi said: this means the nights, the days, the months, and the years.

It was also said: it means the breaths they draw in the world until the term that was appointed for their punishment. His saying, exalted and majestic is He, ﴿The Day We will gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, that is: mention to them, O Muhammad, the day on which those who feared God in the world by obeying Him will be gathered to the Most Merciful, to His Garden, ﴿as a delegation﴾, that is, in groups. "Wafd" (delegation) is the plural of "wafid," like "rakib" and "rakb," and "sahib" and "sahb."

Ibn Abbas said: riding. Abu Hurairah said: upon camels.

Ali ibn Abi Talib said: By God, they will not be gathered on their feet, but upon she-camels whose saddles are gold and whose finest saddle-cloths are rubies; if they wish to go, they go, and if they wish to fly, they fly. [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Kafi al-Shaf" p. (108): "Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abdullah ibn Ahmad in the Zawa'id of the Musnad, al-Tabari, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq ibn al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd ibn Ali, in similar wording. Ibn Abi Dawud recorded it in Kitab al-Ba'th through this route as a marfu' report (traced to the Prophet). Ibn Adi narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, also as a marfu' report." See also "Tafsir Ibn Kathir" 3/138–139, which contains a number of reports on this.]]

﴿And We will drive the criminals﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿to Hell as a thirsty herd﴾, that is, on foot. It was also said: thirsty, their necks having been severed by thirst. "Warid" (thirsty herd) refers to a group that comes to water, and no one comes to water except after thirst.

﴿They will not possess intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾, meaning: none but one who says, "There is no god but God."

It was also said: the meaning is that the intercessors will not intercede except for one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, meaning the believers, as in His saying: "They do not intercede except for one whom He approves" (al-Anbiya' 21:28).

It was also said: none will intercede except one who testifies that there is no god but God, that is, only the believer will intercede. [[All these aspects are true, and each is supported by noble verses and noble hadiths. The criminals do not possess intercession, meaning they do not deserve that any intercessor intercede for them to deliver them from the terror and punishment they are in; and all the more so, the criminals cannot intercede for others, since if they do not deserve intercession for themselves because of their disbelief, their intercession for others is forbidden all the more. Likewise, only the believers who have taken a covenant with God, the Exalted, through the testimony of monotheism and through righteous deeds, and what is similar to this, possess intercession; some of them intercede for others, as God the Exalted said: "On that Day, intercession will not benefit except one whom the Most Merciful permits and whose word He approves" (Ta-Ha 20:109). It has been made clear in other places that the objects they worship besides God do not possess intercession, and that whoever bears witness to the truth possesses it by God's permission to him in that, as in His saying: "Those they invoke besides God do not possess intercession, except those who testify to the truth" (al-Zukhruf 43:86). See "Adwa' al-Bayan" 4/494–495, and consult Ibn Kathir 3/139 and al-Qurtubi 11/154.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 19, verses 97–98:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿So We have made it easy in your tongue﴾, meaning: We made the Qur'an easy by means of your tongue, O Muhammad, ﴿that you may give good tidings thereby to the mindful (muttaqin)﴾, meaning the believers, ﴿and warn thereby a people given to contention (qawman ludda)﴾, meaning fierce in disputation. "Ludd" is the plural of "al-aladd" (the one most stubborn in dispute).

Al-Hasan said: deaf to the truth. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 16/134.]]

Mujahid said: "al-aladd" is the wrongdoer who does not go straight. [[Al-Tabari: 16/133-134.]]

Abu 'Ubayda said: "al-aladd" is the one who does not accept the truth and claims falsehood.

﴿And how many generations We have destroyed before them! Do you perceive any one of them, or hear from them a faint sound?﴾ Meaning: do you see any one of them? It was also said: do you find any one of them? ﴿Or hear from them a faint sound (rikz)﴾, meaning a sound. "Rikz" is a faint sound, as the poet Labid ibn Rabi'a al-'Amiri said: "Then she was startled by the mention of a companion, and it alarmed her, from a distant place, while the companion was her sickness..." [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/135.]] Al-Hasan said: they all perished, so not a trace or a sign of them remained. [[Narrated by 'Abd ibn Humayd in similar wording. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/547.]]
